en: The Analysis of the Bhikkhunī Rules,
2.13 Section on Origination (Samuṭṭhānavāra) By how many of the six origins of offenses do the offenses conditioned by consenting to physical contact originate?
The offenses conditioned by consenting to physical contact originate from one of the six origins of offenses: they originate from one origin.
They originate from both body and mind, not from speech …pe….
Regarding the offenses caused by asking for curd and then eating it: of the six origins of offenses, through how many origins do they originate?
Regarding the offenses caused by asking for curd and then eating it: of the six origins of offenses, they originate through four origins.
There may be [an action] that originates from the body, not from speech or mind;
there may be [an action] that originates from both body and speech, not from the mind;
there may be [an action] that originates from both body and mind, not from speech.
They may originate from body, speech, and mind.
The fifth chapter on origination is finished.
